_comment: Conformance vectors for the turn-capture truncation contract, replayed by
every implementation of it. Four exist and cannot be collapsed: the client
core (packages/memini-client/src/capture.ts) is the canonical one, but the
opencode plugin, hermes, and the Open WebUI filter all ship standalone with
no build step and so carry their own copies.
This file is what keeps them the same function. Without it each copy's own
tests asserted its own behaviour and all four passed while disagreeing --
the client core destroyed the text on a NaN cap while the opencode copy
returned it whole, and nothing noticed. Modelled on derivation-vectors.json,
which pins deriveLocalNamespace the same way.
Add a case here first, then make every implementation pass it.
marker is appended verbatim on a cut; `null` for `max` stands in for any
non-numeric value a language can express (JS null/undefined, Python None).

cases.name: under the cap: untouched and unmarked
exactly at the cap: untouched and unmarked
one over the cap: cut and marked
empty text stays empty and unmarked
counts characters, not UTF-8 bytes: 3 CJK chars are 9 bytes
CJK under the cap by characters, over it by bytes
astral characters are never split: 2 emoji are 4 UTF-16 code units
a cap landing exactly on the emoji count does not cut
mixed ascii and astral counts by character
non-numeric cap fails open: store the text rather than destroy it
cases.text: the entire user turn, every word of it
cases.expect: the entire user turn, every word of it
